pool.text: The historic town of Dover later figured prominently in the Domesday Book.
Edward Hasted reported that the town had a population of almost 10,000 people.
The South Eastern Railway's main line connected the town with Folkestone.
The London, Chatham and Dover Railway opened its line from Canterbury.
Louis Blériot landed his aircraft here after completing the first cross-Channel flight.
The former cinema King's Hall first opened and is now a bingo club.
The Chatham Main Line into Priory was electrified under British Railways modernization.
The Gateway Hospital Broadcasting Service was founded as the oldest hospital radio in East Kent.
An important archaeological discovery was made at Langdon Bay off the coast.
The ancient Bronze Age Dover boat was discovered six metres deep underwater.
The White Cliffs Theatre opened and is based at Astor College.
P&O Ferries sailings to Zeebrugge were permanently withdrawn from the harbour.
Hoverspeed ceased its operations and withdrew all eight of its daily sailings.
SpeedFerries officially ceased operations and withdrew their daily cross-channel sailings.
The St James' retail area opened as part of transformations to the town.
Thousands of tourists visited the historic castle located in the town.
A long line of freight trucks formed due to sudden border closures with France.
Dover Community Radio started broadcasting on its community radio frequency.
The town had an estimated population of over forty-four thousand residents.
